citations.description: Ticket status field shows 'open'; the comment says 'Closing as not_a_bug per the rebar-debug not-a-bug guard' but the ticket was not actually transitioned.

findings.criterion: Classify explicitly: defect vs intended-behavior vs authoring convention. If intended, close as not-a-bug with the citation and, if useful, document the commit-message wrapping convention instead.
findings.detail: The investigation comment classifies the issue as 'NOT a defect — intended-behavior / authoring convention' with detailed citations (change 982, bimodal line-length data, zero injection-site matches). However, the ticket status remains 'open' rather than closed as not-a-bug, which the criterion explicitly requires. The documentary follow-up (adding the ~72-column convention to CONTRIBUTING.md) is also recommended in the comment but not confirmed as done.
findings.remediation: Transition the ticket status to not_a_bug / closed. Optionally add the ~72-column commit-body wrapping convention to CONTRIBUTING.md as the comment recommends.
findings.title: Ticket not closed as not-a-bug despite classification being complete

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
